title: Determining the hydroxylation status of NAA10-Trp38
projectDescription: NAA10 is the major human N-terminal acetyltransferase (NAT). The KAT activity of NAA10 towards hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) was recently reported to depend on the hydroxylation at Trp38 of NAA10 by factor inhibiting HIF-1α (FIH). As a consequence, Trp38 hydroxylation status was proposed to act as a general NAA10-switch between its NAT and KAT state. We attempted to quantify the degree of hydroxylation of NAA10. We could not detect any hydroxylation of Trp38 of NAA10 in several human cell lines.
sampleProcessingProtocol: NAA10 or NAA15 immunoprecipitated from HEK293, HeLa and HAP1 cells were analyzed for interactors and hydroxylation at tryptophan, aspartate and asparagine residues. IPs were digested with trypsin and LysC using either FASP or in-solution digestion, and analyzed by either a 3-hour method on a QExactive-HF (FASP samples) or a 30-minute method on an Exploris 480 (in-solution samples).
dataProcessingProtocol: RAW files were searched in Maxquant 1.6.17.0 with fixed Cys carbamidomethylation and variable oxidation (+16 Da) of Met, Asn, Asp, or Trp. Peptides were quantified by intensity and protein groups by iBAQ.
